items.title: Allen Toussaint Interview, 1979-03-13
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ... Frank Butler. Well, thank you very much, Alan Toussaint.

ctx.x: Seven, nine. Like Ellis and myself, of course.

And James Rivers is doing some really good things again. Yes, yes. He's so authentic. Frank Butler. Well, thank you very much, Alan Toussaint. It's been a real pleasure and a real honor having you here with our WTUL audience.

dear Mike Wooden-Joe, Walter Blue. Oh man, I wish I could call him. I wish I could sit down and call him that bus. Who did you used to hang around with when you were a kid? Sidney Basham, I'll say? Me and Michelle was party one. When you see me, you see him. He'd get home in the morning, leave home, he'd come to my house and we'd be together every day. Was he older than you or younger than you? No, Michelle was younger than me. Uh huh. Yeah. Did we get the year you were born, eh? Yeah, I was born.
